articles.title: Skolefraværet går nedover
articles.content:
Fraværet i norsk videregående skole ble forrige skoleår redusert med to dager sammenlignet med året før. Det er også en markant nedgang i antall elever som er borte fra skolen mer enn ti dager i skoleåret, skriver Kunnskapsdepartementet i en pressemelding.

Dette er første gang etter pandemien at fraværet går nedover.

Regjeringa gir nye fråværsreglar æra for at fråværet har gått ned. – Funkar for dei ressurssterke, ikkje elevane som har det tungt, seier Elevorganisasjonen.

Fraværsgrense i skolen

Det samlede fraværet i den videregående skolen har gått kraftig ned etter innføringen av fraværsgrensen. Tall for skoleåret 2016-2017 viser at fraværet falt med 30 prosent. Nedgangen var størst for yrkesfag.

articles.content:

Ordfører Vitali Klitschko sier russiske missiler har rammet en høyblokk og at redningsmannskaper er på stedet.

articles.content:
Andreas Sjalg Unneland sier han har bestemt seg for å takke nei til å bli en del av SV-ledelsen.

Han er regnet som en av favorittene som SV-nestleder.

Nylig ble det klart at SV-nestleder Marian Hussein ikke ønsker gjenvalg. Det gjør heller ikke partisekretær Audun Herning, som gir seg etter ti år i vervet.

13 av 22 tillitsvalgte i SVs øverste organer ønsker ikke gjenvalg, viser en oversikt NRK har fått tilgang til.

articles.title: Today in Norway: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
articles.content:
Add a comment

                        Norwegian politicians face online harassment over immigration, Queen Sonja is no longer listed as a member of the Royal House of Norway, Christmas products hit supermarkets, and more news on Tuesday.

Norwegian politicians face online harassment, especially over immigration

A recent report from the think tank Agenda shows that online attacks against Norwegian politicians have gone up by almost 50 percent in the past few years.

"Go to hell, you bitch", "disgusting liars", and "go to hell, you misshapen oaf" are just a few of the thousands of abusive comments Norwegian politicians have received on social media, according to the report.

The study looked at 3.8 million comments from 76 members of parliament and found that Labour Party politicians face the highest volume of attacks, with the majority classified as cyberthreats.

"The debate on social media has become tougher and more demanding for many politicians. It is obviously very unpleasant for those involved, but it is also turning into a big social problem," said Thea Joramo Lysne, communications manager at the Agenda think tank.

"The number of attacks in politicians' comment sections has increased over time and, in the worst case, it can lead to politicians quitting or stop people from standing for election. We can't afford that in a democracy, where we need more than 10,000 elected officials in municipal councils, county councils, and the Storting," she added.

The study also found that debates about immigration and integration get the most hostile reactions. These topics show up almost three times more often in the harshest posts compared to other posts by politicians.

Queen Sonja no longer listed as member of the Royal House

On the Royal Court's official website, Queen Sonja is no longer listed as a member of the Royal House (Det kongelige hus).

The update took effect as the period of court mourning concluded and the website transitioned back from mourning mode to standard operations, replacing the main portrait of King Harald with King Haakon and Queen Mette-Marit.

“The Royal House includes the current monarch and their spouses and the next of kin in subsequent generations and their spouses. The term royal family also includes the monarch's other family,” the Palace website clarifies.

The Royal House now consists of King Haakon, Queen Mette-Marit, and Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra.

​Norwegian vocabulary: deres Majesteter - their majesties

Even though there are still almost 80 days until Christmas, festive products have already started showing up on supermarket shelves across Norway.

It's common for retailers to stock seasonal products well ahead of winter, with julebrus (christmas soda) being among the most iconic. However, their early arrival has started the usual debate about whether holiday shopping starts too soon, especially since Halloween is still weeks away.

While shoppers remain divided over seeing holiday items in mid-October, many enthusiasts are eager to buy them.

Beverage producer Ringnes defended the early launch in an email to business outlet E24, saying fans look forward to it every year.

The company also explained that they sold around ten million litres of Christmas soda last year alone, with production remaining at similar levels this season.

"For Christmas soda enthusiasts, this doesn't come a day too early. We know that many have been waiting to open the first Christmas soda of the year," said Ringnes Christmas soda manager Ida Lyche Sørensen in a press release. "Christmas soda is more than just a soft drink. It's Christmas spirit in bottles and cans. For many, that first taste marks the very start of Christmas."

A security guard at the United States Embassy in Oslo has been charged by Norway’s economic crime authority, Økokrim, with tax evasion of about 780,000 kroner, according to the newspaper Aftenposten.

Investigators said the alleged tax evasion happened over five years, from 2021 to 2025.

The verdict is still pending, and the US Embassy has declined to comment on the case.

Nunna Moum from Larvik just celebrated her 111th birthday on Monday, reaching another milestone as Norway's oldest living person.

"I'm supposedly the oldest in the country. I don't really think anything special about it," Moum told Norwegian newspaper VG. However, she showed her warm and playful side in the interview, quickly adding, "Someone has to be the oldest too! I can't just lie down either!"

articles.title: MI5-sjefen: Mistenkte iranske terrorplaner mot flybase ikke et enkelttilfelle
articles.content:
Iran forsøker å intensivere angrepene mot Storbritannia og ramme nye mål, etter tidligere primært å ha gått etter regimekritiske iranere, sier MI5-sjef Ken McCallum.

Det var 27. september at tre mistenkelige varebiler ble stoppet nær flybasen RAF Fairford i Gloucestershire sørvest i England. Politi gjorde funn av bensin i varebilene, men ingen eksplosiver. Sju menn i 20-årene ble pågrepet, løslatt mot kausjon og er under etterforskning.

Den britiske regjeringen mener iranske myndigheter sto bak, noe Iran avviser. Den mistenkte angrepsplanen «er ikke unik», ifølge McCallum.

Flybasen har lenge blitt brukt som base for amerikanske bombefly, og de siste månedene har flyene deltatt i krigen mot Iran.

Iran

Iran er en islamsk republikk i Midtøsten. Siden 28. februar har landet vært i krig med USA og Israel. Samtidig har det siden slutten av 2025 vært store demonstrasjoner mot det ultrakonservative, undertrykkende regimet i landet.

articles.content:

                        Norway's data protection authority on Monday slapped a 92 million kroner (8.6 million euro) fine on Microsoft subsidiary Xandr for sharing user-data from dating app Grindr.

Xandr, an online advertising company, is accused of processing and then transmitting data from Grindr users to a real-time advertising bidding system, where it may have been shared with potentially thousands of companies to enable them to display targeted ads.

Datatilsynet said thousands of Norwegian users of the app had been affected after information that could reveal their sexual orientation was passed on to advertisers without their explicit consent.

"The violations in this case are very serious," said Datatilsynet chief Line Coll.

"Responsibility for data protection cannot be delegated to others. Each company must itself ensure, and be able to prove, that it is authorised to use this data."

Xandr said it believed Grindr had previously obtained its users' consent.

The violations occurred between July 2018 and April 2020 before the firm was bought by Microsoft.

The Norwegian courts in 2025 upheld a Datatilsynet fine of 65 million kroner on Grindr for unlawfully sharing sensitive data.

articles.title: 'The world’s loneliest place': Norway ranked the 'hardest country to make friends'
articles.content:
Add a comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            Norway has been ranked as the hardest country in the world for foreign residents to make friends, according to the 2026 InterNations survey. Photo by Noah Silliman on Unsplash
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        It’s official: Norway has been ranked as the hardest country in the world for international residents to settle in and build a social life, according to a major global survey. But does this really come as a surprise?

Norway landed at the bottom of the rankings in the latest InterNations survey, which is based on responses from thousands of foreign citizens living around the world.

“Norway finishes 31st out of 31 destinations in 2026. Expats there are the unhappiest in the survey,” the report said, adding that Norway is "the world’s loneliest place".

Whilst the country scored well in the category of Environment and Climate, it was ranked dead last for Ease of Settling In.

This category considered how friendly the locals were in general, how easy it was to make friends with them and whether foreigners find it easy to feel at home in the country.

A significant 72 percent of respondents said making local friends is difficult, which is over 30 percentage points higher than the global average of 40 percent.

"It’s telling that around half (51 percent) describe their friends and acquaintances as mostly other expats (vs 37 percent globally)," the report said, adding that only a quarter (25 percent) are content with their social life in the country (vs 54 percent globally).

READ MORE: Five tips to help you make more friends and combat loneliness in Norway

Fewer than two in five foreigners living in Norway find the local population friendly in general (37 percent vs 63 percent globally) and towards foreign residents specifically (37 percent vs 61 percent).

This lack of social integration and the difficulties it creates, combined with other factors like limited job openings, brutal costs, and a feeling of "having little to do" leaves many foreign residents feeling unhappy with their life.

Less than half of respondents (46 percent) are content with life in Norway, which is much lower than the 70 percent global average.

READ ALSO: Five places to find a sense of community in Norway

When asked if they feel at home in the country, only 31 percent said that they do, compared to 61 percent globally. "Expats feel neither at home nor welcome in Norway," the report concluded.

The struggle for foreign residents to settle in and make friends in Norway is nothing new, the country has been ranked in the bottom 10 for Ease of Settling In for the seventh year in a row.

"I dislike the cost and difficulty of making friends. It’s a lonely country to live in," said a British resident living in Bærum, quoted in the report.

So is it that hard to make friends with locals in Norway? Share your experiences in the comments below.

articles.title: Burnham: Russland blanda seg inn i Brexit-avstemminga
articles.content:
Storbritannias statsminister Andy Burnham seier at Russland blanda seg inn i Brexit-avstemminga i 2016.

Burnham er den første britiske statsministeren som opent seier at det er bevis på russisk innblanding i folkeavstemminga for ti år sidan, skriv Reuters.

– Då eg kom til Downing Street stilte eg spørsmålet: Var det innblanding i folkeavstemminga i 2016 frå Russland? Og eg har gått det klare svaret at ja, det var det, sa Burnham i eit intervju med podkasten The Rest is Politics som vart publisert søndag.

Burnham sa ingenting om korleis han meinte at Russland hadde blanda seg inn i folkeavstemminga.

Tidlegare statsminister Boris Johnson sa i 2020 at det ikkje var noko bevis på russisk innblanding i avstemminga.

I ein rapport frå 2020 klarte ikkje regjeringa i Storbritannia å slå fast om Russland blanda seg inn. Men rapporten slo fast at Russland prøvde å påverke Skottlands sjølvstendeavstemming i 2014, skriv Reuters.

Det opplyser guvernør Josh Shapiro lørdag. Flere av de drepte skal være barn. Skuddene skal ha skjedd i og utenfor en bolig.

– Jeg har ikke sett noe lignende på mine 28-pluss år, sier politisjef Rick Lorah i Erie til en lokal nyhetskanal.

Lorah ønsket ikke å gi flere detaljer, men sa at omstendighetene rundt skytingen var «dypt urovekkende».

Shapiro opplyste lørdag at han tilbød administrasjonens «fulle støtte» til Eries ordfører Daria Devlin.

De lokale myndighetene i Erie opplyste sent fredag kveld at den mistenkte gjerningsmannen var død og at det ikke var noen trussel mot offentligheten.

Erie er en by på rundt 102.000 innbyggere, rundt 206 kilometer nord for Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Trump angriper Zelenskyj
articles.content:
Trump sier Ukraina må stoppe å angripe russiske oljeraffinerier. Han mener også at Ukraina trenger en ny president.

Fredag sa Trump at han hadde inngått en avtale med Putin om at Russland skal selge diesel til USA.

– Det er et motsatt signal fra det vi trenger nå. Vestlige land har stått sammen om å stramme til sanksjonene mot Russland, nettopp på olje- og oljeprodukter som er den viktiges, kommenterte utenriksminister Espen Barth Eide.

Ukraina har gjennomført flere angrep mot russiske oljeraffinerier i høst. Zelenskyj varslet i forrige uke at Ukraina vil trappe opp slike angrep.

Russland gikk til full krig mot Ukraina i 2022, og har siden gjennomført regelmessige angrep mot ukrainske energianlegg.

Krigen i Ukraina

Russland invaderte Krim og deler av fylkene Luhansk og Donetsk i Øst-Ukraina i 2014. 24. februar 2022 gikk Russland til fullskala invasjon. Krigen medfører store militære tap og rammer sivile hardt.

articles.title: Panamas president: Ingen opplysninger om omkomne
articles.content:
Det er så langt ikke meldt om omkomne etter det kraftige jordskjelvet i Panama fredag.

Det opplyser landets president, José Raúl Mulino, til journalister natt til lørdag.

Han sier at myndighetene som arbeider med å avklare situasjonen, foreløpig ikke har fått meldinger om omkomne.

– Men de er i ferd med å avklare dette, sier Mulino. Han understreker samtidig at det bare er gått få timer siden jordskjelvet.

Skjelvet, som hadde en styrke på 7,7, rammet Panama rundt klokken 20 norsk tid fredag.

– Det er mulig at det er omkomne. Men la oss håpe at det ikke er det, sier presidenten.

Jordskjelv i Mellom-Amerika

Et jordskjelv med en styrke på 7 har truffet 150 kilometer utenfor kysten av Nicaragua og El Salvador. Skjelvet var 10 kilometer dypt, og det er sendt ut tsunamivarsel.
